title: Mapping LLM Capability Frontiers via Formalized and Calibrated Probes

problem.claim: LLM reasoning ability is poorly understood.

gap.claim: Task-level accuracy evaluations can conflate pattern matching with reasoning capability.

contributions.claim: The authors present X-RAY, a reasoning analysis system using calibrated, formally verified probes to map LLM reasoning capability.
The framework models reasoning capability through extractable structure, including constraint interaction, reasoning depth, and solution-space geometry.
X-RAY generates probes with controlled structural variations using formal tools, calibration, and verification.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report a systematic asymmetry: models are relatively robust to constraint refinement but degrade sharply under solution-space restructuring.
The authors report that calibrated formal probes distinguish models that appear indistinguishable on standard benchmarks and expose interpretable failure modes.
The authors report evaluating state-of-the-art LLMs on mathematics, physics, and chemistry problems ranging from junior-level to advanced.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM reasoning ability remains poorly understood.
Existing task-level evaluations may confuse pattern matching with reasoning.
X-RAY uses calibrated, formally verified probes and models reasoning through structural properties.
The framework is applied to state-of-the-art LLMs across mathematics, physics, and chemistry.
The authors report asymmetric robustness, benchmark-discriminating probes, interpretable failures, and potential use for training and testing reasoning models.

source_observation.claim: Models reportedly degrade sharply when structural changes alter the underlying solution manifold.

interpretation.claim: Reasoning evaluations may need to vary solution structure, not only add or remove constraints.

application.claim: Design probes that separately test constraint refinement and solution-space restructuring.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this asymmetry generalizes beyond the evaluated models and problem domains.

source_observation.claim: Calibrated formal probes reportedly distinguish models with similar standard-benchmark performance.

interpretation.claim: Calibration and structural control may reveal capability differences hidden by aggregate benchmark accuracy.

application.claim: Use calibrated probes as supplementary evaluations for reasoning-model training and testing.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the calibration procedure, benchmark comparisons, or validation scope.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the evaluated models, datasets, probe counts, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide details of the formal verification and calibration procedures.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported findings.
